solution:
The vector equation of a line through point \(\bar{a}\) parallel to \(\bar{b}\) is \(\bar{r}=\bar{a}+\lambda\bar{b}\).
Here \(\bar{a}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-7\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{b}=6\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).
\(\therefore \bar{r}=(3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-7\hat{k})+\lambda(6\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})\).

The point \((3,2,1)\) has position vector \(\bar{a}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and the line is parallel to \(\bar{b}=2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\).
Using \(\bar{r}=\bar{a}+\lambda\bar{b}\):
\(\therefore \bar{r}=(3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-3\hat{k})\).

A line parallel to \(\frac{x+2}{3}=\frac{y-3}{5}=\frac{z+5}{6}\) has the same direction ratios \(3,5,6\).
The required line passes through \((-2,4,-5)\), so using \(\frac{x-x_1}{a}=\frac{y-y_1}{b}=\frac{z-z_1}{c}\):
\(\therefore \frac{x+2}{3}=\frac{y-4}{5}=\frac{z+5}{6}\).

Comparing \(\frac{x+5}{3}=\frac{y+4}{5}=\frac{z+5}{6}\) with \(\frac{x-x_1}{a}=\frac{y-y_1}{b}=\frac{z-z_1}{c}\), the line passes through \((-5,-4,-5)\) with direction ratios \(3,5,6\).
So \(\bar{a}=-5\hat{i}-4\hat{j}-5\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{b}=3\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+6\hat{k}\).
\(\therefore \bar{r}=(-5\hat{i}-4\hat{j}-5\hat{k})+\lambda(3\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+6\hat{k})\).

The line passes through the origin \(O\) (\(\bar{a}=\bar{0}\)) and the point \((5,-2,3)\) with position vector \(\bar{b}=5\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\).
Here the direction of the line is \(\bar{b}-\bar{a}=5\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\).
\(\therefore \bar{r}=\bar{0}+\lambda(5\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})\), i.e. \(\bar{r}=\lambda(5\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})\).

For points \(A(3,-2,-5)\) and \(B(3,-2,6)\), direction ratios of \(AB\) are
\((3-3,\,-2-(-2),\,6-(-5))=(0,0,11)\), i.e. proportional to \(0,0,1\).
Using \(A(3,-2,-5)\):
\(\therefore \frac{x-3}{0}=\frac{y+2}{0}=\frac{z+5}{11}\), which means \(x=3,\ y=-2\) (the line is parallel to the Z-axis).

The line is perpendicular to both \(\bar{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{c}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}\), so its direction is \(\bar{b}\times\bar{c}\).
\(\bar{b}\times\bar{c}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&2&1\\3&2&-1\end{vmatrix}=\hat{i}(2(-1)-1\cdot2)-\hat{j}(1\cdot(-1)-1\cdot3)+\hat{k}(1\cdot2-2\cdot3)\)
\(=-4\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-4\hat{k}\), proportional to \(1,-1,1\).
Using \(A(1,1,2)\):
\(\therefore \frac{x-1}{1}=\frac{y-1}{-1}=\frac{z-2}{1}\).

The line is perpendicular to the given lines whose direction ratios are \(1,2,3\) and \(-3,2,5\), so its direction is their cross product.
\(\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&2&3\\-3&2&5\end{vmatrix}=\hat{i}(2\cdot5-3\cdot2)-\hat{j}(1\cdot5-3(-3))+\hat{k}(1\cdot2-2(-3))\)
\(=4\hat{i}-14\hat{j}+8\hat{k}\), proportional to \(2,-7,4\).
Using \((2,1,3)\):
\(\therefore \frac{x-2}{2}=\frac{y-1}{-7}=\frac{z-3}{4}\).

Write the given line \(x-1=y-2=z-3=t\); a general point is \(P(1+t,\,2+t,\,3+t)\) and its direction ratios are \(1,1,1\).
The required line joins the origin \(O\) to \(P\), so its direction is \(\overline{OP}=(1+t)\hat{i}+(2+t)\hat{j}+(3+t)\hat{k}\).
For a right angle, \(\overline{OP}\) is perpendicular to \((1,1,1)\):
\((1+t)+(2+t)+(3+t)=0\Rightarrow 6+3t=0\Rightarrow t=-2\).
Then \(P=(-1,0,1)\), so \(\overline{OP}=-\hat{i}+\hat{k}\).
\(\therefore \bar{r}=\lambda(-\hat{i}+\hat{k})\).

Reduce each line to symmetric form to read direction ratios.
Line 1: \(\frac{1-x}{3}=\frac{x-1}{-3}\); \(\frac{7y-14}{2\lambda}=\frac{y-2}{2\lambda/7}\); \(\frac{z-3}{2}\). Direction ratios: \(-3,\ \frac{2\lambda}{7},\ 2\).
Line 2: \(\frac{7-7x}{3\lambda}=\frac{x-1}{-3\lambda/7}\); \(\frac{y-5}{1}\); \(\frac{6-z}{5}=\frac{z-6}{-5}\). Direction ratios: \(-\frac{3\lambda}{7},\ 1,\ -5\).
Lines are perpendicular \(\Rightarrow\) sum of products of direction ratios \(=0\):
\((-3)\left(-\frac{3\lambda}{7}\right)+\frac{2\lambda}{7}(1)+(2)(-5)=0\)
\(\frac{9\lambda}{7}+\frac{2\lambda}{7}-10=0\Rightarrow\frac{11\lambda}{7}=10\)
\(\therefore \lambda=\frac{70}{11}\).

Direction vectors: \(\bar{b_1}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{b_2}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).
\(\bar{b_1}\cdot\bar{b_2}=(1)(2)+(-1)(1)+(2)(1)=3\).
\(|\bar{b_1}|=\sqrt{1+1+4}=\sqrt{6}\), \(|\bar{b_2}|=\sqrt{4+1+1}=\sqrt{6}\).
\(\cos\theta=\frac{|\bar{b_1}\cdot\bar{b_2}|}{|\bar{b_1}||\bar{b_2}|}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{6}\sqrt{6}}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac{1}{2}\).
\(\therefore \theta=60^\circ\).

Line 1: \(x=y,\ z=0\). A point on it is \((t,t,0)\), so its direction ratios are \(1,1,0\); \(\bar{b_1}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}\).
Line 2: \(x=0,\ z=0\) is the Y-axis, direction ratios \(0,1,0\); \(\bar{b_2}=\hat{j}\).
\(\cos\theta=\frac{|\bar{b_1}\cdot\bar{b_2}|}{|\bar{b_1}||\bar{b_2}|}=\frac{|1|}{\sqrt{2}\cdot1}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\).
\(\therefore \theta=45^\circ\).

Line 1: \(x=-y,\ z=0\). A point on it is \((t,-t,0)\), so its direction ratios are \(1,-1,0\); \(\bar{b_1}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}\).
Line 2: \(x=0,\ z=0\) is the Y-axis, direction ratios \(0,1,0\); \(\bar{b_2}=\hat{j}\).
\(\cos\theta=\frac{|\bar{b_1}\cdot\bar{b_2}|}{|\bar{b_1}||\bar{b_2}|}=\frac{|-1|}{\sqrt{2}\cdot1}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\).
\(\therefore \theta=45^\circ\).

Reduce \(2x-2=3y+1=6z-2\) to symmetric form. Write each factor as \(a(\cdot)\):
\(2x-2=2(x-1),\ 3y+1=3\left(y+\frac{1}{3}\right),\ 6z-2=6\left(z-\frac{1}{3}\right)\).
So \(\frac{x-1}{1/2}=\frac{y+1/3}{1/3}=\frac{z-1/3}{1/6}\); multiplying denominators by \(6\) gives direction ratios \(3,2,1\).
The required line passes through \((-1,-1,2)\) parallel to \(3,2,1\).
Vector form: \(\bar{r}=(-\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+\lambda(3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})\).
Cartesian form: \(\frac{x+1}{3}=\frac{y+1}{2}=\frac{z-2}{1}\).

Comparing \(\bar{r}=\left(-2\hat{i}+\frac{5}{2}\hat{j}-\hat{k}\right)+\lambda(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j})\) with \(\bar{r}=\bar{a}+\lambda\bar{b}\), the direction vector is \(\bar{b}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+0\hat{k}\).
\(|\bar{b}|=\sqrt{2^2+3^2+0^2}=\sqrt{13}\).
Direction cosines \(=\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}},\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}},\ 0\right)\).

The required line passes through the origin, so its direction is the position vector of the point where it meets the second line.
Any point on \(\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+1}{3}=\frac{z-1}{4}=s\) is \(P(1+2s,\,-1+3s,\,1+4s)\).
Direction of \(\overline{OP}\) is \((1+2s,\,-1+3s,\,1+4s)\). It must be perpendicular to the first line (direction ratios \(1,1,1\)):
\((1+2s)+(-1+3s)+(1+4s)=0\Rightarrow 1+9s=0\Rightarrow s=-\frac{1}{9}\).
Then \(P=\left(\frac{7}{9},\,-\frac{4}{3},\,\frac{5}{9}\right)\), so \(\overline{OP}\) is proportional to \(7,-12,5\).
\(\therefore \frac{x}{7}=\frac{y}{-12}=\frac{z}{5}\).

The line is the intersection of the planes \(y=2\) and \(4x-3z+5=0\), so its direction is perpendicular to both plane-normals \(\bar{n_1}=\hat{j}\) and \(\bar{n_2}=4\hat{i}-3\hat{k}\).
\(\bar{b}=\bar{n_1}\times\bar{n_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\0&1&0\\4&0&-3\end{vmatrix}=-3\hat{i}+0\hat{j}-4\hat{k}\), take \(\bar{b}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{k}\).
A point on the line: take \(x=1\Rightarrow 4-3z+5=0\Rightarrow z=3\), with \(y=2\); so \(A(1,2,3)\).
\(\therefore \bar{r}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})+\lambda(3\hat{i}+4\hat{k})\).

Using \(\bar{r}=\bar{a}+\lambda\bar{b}\) with \(\bar{a}=-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{b}=4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\):
\(\therefore \bar{r}=(-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})+\lambda(4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\).

Let \(\bar{a}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-7\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{b}=6\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) be the position vectors of the two points.
Direction of the line \(=\bar{b}-\bar{a}=(6-3)\hat{i}+(-1-4)\hat{j}+(1+7)\hat{k}=3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+8\hat{k}\).
Using \(\bar{r}=\bar{a}+\lambda(\bar{b}-\bar{a})\):
\(\therefore \bar{r}=(3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-7\hat{k})+\lambda(3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+8\hat{k})\).

Direction ratios \(-3,4,2\) give the direction vector \(\bar{b}=-3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\), and \(\bar{a}=5\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\).
Using \(\bar{r}=\bar{a}+\lambda\bar{b}\):
\(\therefore \bar{r}=(5\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+3\hat{k})+\lambda(-3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\).

The line is perpendicular to \(\bar{p}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{q}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}\), so its direction is \(\bar{p}\times\bar{q}\).
\(\bar{p}\times\bar{q}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&1&1\\2&-1&1\end{vmatrix}=\hat{i}(1+1)-\hat{j}(1-2)+\hat{k}(-1-2)=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\).
With \(\bar{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\):
\(\therefore \bar{r}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\hat{k})\).

A line parallel to \(\bar{r}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})+\lambda(3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})\) has the same direction \(\bar{b}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).
With \(\bar{a}=-\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\):
\(\therefore \bar{r}=(-\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+\lambda(3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})\).

Using \(\frac{x-x_1}{a}=\frac{y-y_1}{b}=\frac{z-z_1}{c}\) with \(A(-1,2,1)\) and direction ratios \(2,3,1\):
\(\therefore \frac{x+1}{2}=\frac{y-2}{3}=\frac{z-1}{1}\).

Direction ratios of \(AB=(1-(-2),\ 1-3,\ 2-4)=(3,-2,-2)\).
Equation of line \(AB\) through \(A(-2,3,4)\):
\(\frac{x+2}{3}=\frac{y-3}{-2}=\frac{z-4}{-2}\).
To test \(C(4,-1,0)\), substitute its coordinates:
\(\frac{4+2}{3}=2,\quad \frac{-1-3}{-2}=2,\quad \frac{0-4}{-2}=2\).
All three ratios are equal (\(=2\)), so \(C\) lies on line \(AB\).
\(\therefore A,B,C\) are collinear.

Line 1: point \((-1,-3,4)\), direction \((-10,-1,1)\); general point \(P=(-1-10t,\,-3-t,\,4+t)\).
Line 2: point \((-10,-1,1)\), direction \((-1,-3,4)\); general point \(Q=(-10-s,\,-1-3s,\,1+4s)\).
Equate coordinates for a common point:
From \(x\): \(-1-10t=-10-s\Rightarrow s=10t-9\).
From \(y\): \(-3-t=-1-3s\Rightarrow s=\frac{2+t}{3}\).
Solving: \(10t-9=\frac{2+t}{3}\Rightarrow 30t-27=2+t\Rightarrow 29t=29\Rightarrow t=1\), giving \(s=1\).
Check \(z\): \(4+t=5\) and \(1+4s=5\) — satisfied, so the lines intersect.
Point of intersection \(=(-1-10,\,-3-1,\,4+1)=(-11,-4,5)\).

The line is perpendicular to the two given lines whose directions are \(\bar{b_1}=2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{b_2}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\); so its direction is \(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}\).
\(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\2&-2&1\\1&-2&2\end{vmatrix}=\hat{i}(-4+2)-\hat{j}(4-1)+\hat{k}(-4+2)=-2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\), proportional to \(2,3,2\).
With \(\bar{a}=3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\):
Vector form: \(\bar{r}=(3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\).
Cartesian form: \(\frac{x-3}{2}=\frac{y+1}{3}=\frac{z-2}{2}\).

To show the line \(\frac{x-2}{1}=\frac{y-4}{2}=\frac{z+4}{-2}\) passes through the origin, substitute \((0,0,0)\):
\(\frac{0-2}{1}=-2,\quad \frac{0-4}{2}=-2,\quad \frac{0+4}{-2}=-2\).
All three expressions are equal (\(=-2\)), so \((0,0,0)\) satisfies the equation of the line.
\(\therefore\) the line passes through the origin.
